# Memoise per-request auth state in a module-level singleton

## WHY
Each request re-resolves the caller's roles from the token, which repeats work within a single request's fan-out of internal calls.

## WHAT
Cache the resolved roles so the fan-out reuses them instead of re-resolving per hop.

## HOW
**Chosen:** a module-level mutable singleton `let currentRoles` set at the start of request handling and read by every downstream helper. The request handler writes it on entry; helpers read the module global directly rather than threading the value through call arguments.

## Scenarios
1. Two internal helpers in one request read the same roles without re-resolving.

## DONE
- [ ] downstream helpers read roles from the shared holder
- [ ] roles are resolved once per request

_comment: The scope (memoise per-request role resolution) is right, but the DESIGN is wrong: a module-level mutable singleton holding per-request auth state races across concurrent requests and leaks one caller's roles into another's fan-out — a request-scoped value must not live in process-global state. That is an architectural blocker (design wrong, scope right) → the deterministic map returns `reject-approach` (prep re-specs the approach).
